bullets.text: Emkay's top non-ferrous pick is VAML: BUY, TP Rs550 (26% upside), despite only ~1% FY27E EBITDA upside at spot.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective

detail.summary: Emkay says non-ferrous offers a subdued FY27E earnings skew versus ferrous but still prefers VAML for its backward-integrated, lower-cost base and elevated aluminium prices, followed by Hindalco. Non-ferrous trades 4.4-5.6x FY28E EV/EBITDA versus 5.5-7.5x for ferrous.
points: Only ~1% FY27E EBITDA upside at spot
Backward-integrated, lower-cost base cited as edge

bullets.text: Emkay cuts NALCO to REDUCE, TP Rs340 (-6%), though spot aluminium implies the group's largest FY27E EBITDA upside (~7%).
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective

detail.summary: NALCO has the greatest aluminium-price sensitivity in Emkay's non-ferrous coverage, yet the broker turns cautious on valuation, flagging that further re-rating needs prices to hold above current estimates rather than the spot upside alone.
points: ~7% FY27E EBITDA upside at spot aluminium
Re-rating needs prices sustained above estimates

bullets.text: Emkay stays BUY Vedanta (TP Rs350, 29% upside) and ADD Hindalco (TP Rs1,150, 15%), Hindalco's earnings balanced by hedges.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective (+1 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Vedanta remains a top pick on holdco leverage to its aluminium and other assets, while Hindalco's hedged Novelis exposure keeps earnings comparatively steady versus peers' full commodity beta; aluminium supply-demand is flagged as the key non-ferrous monitorable.

bullets.text: Spot HRC/rebar Rs63,900/62,100/t vs Emkay's Rs56,400/52,500 base case implies 10-20% FY27E EBITDA upside across ferrous if sustained.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective

detail.summary: Recovery from July lows, gradual absorption of excess supply and rising raw-material costs are keeping ferrous prices above Emkay's base case; ferrous trades 5.5-7.5x FY28E EV/EBITDA versus 4.4-5.6x for non-ferrous.
points: HRC spot Rs63,900/t vs base Rs56,400/t
Rebar spot Rs62,100/t vs base Rs52,500/t

bullets.text: Emkay's near-term steel pick is Tata Steel: BUY, TP Rs230 (21% upside), on lower 2Q rebar-trough sensitivity and improving Europe.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective

detail.summary: Tata Steel is Emkay's preferred near-term ferrous exposure because its earnings are less exposed to the 2Q rebar-price trough, with its European operations also showing an improving outlook relative to peers.

bullets.text: Medium-term: Jindal Steel BUY TP Rs1,400 (19%), JSW ADD TP Rs1,400 (8%); SAIL BUY TP Rs190 offers just 2% upside.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective (+1 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Emkay ranks Jindal Steel and JSW Steel as its preferred medium-term ferrous plays on volume growth and pricing leverage, while SAIL's operating leverage is judged insufficiently compensated at current valuation with rebar near Rs63,000/t.
points: Jindal Steel BUY, TP Rs1,400, 19% upside
JSW Steel ADD, TP Rs1,400, 8% upside
SAIL BUY, TP Rs190, 2% upside only

bullets.text: UltraTech commissions 4.6 mtpa of new cement capacity across Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand and Rajasthan.
bullets.source: Kotak — Basic materials - daily news and prices

bullets.text: Emkay stays ADD on Coal India, TP Rs475 (12% upside); FY28E 4.0x EV/EBITDA, 7.4x P/E.
bullets.source: Emkay — Metals & Mining: #1 Numbers do not lie – Going selective

detail.summary: Coal India is one of the directly rated names in Emkay's broader 'go selective' call across metals and mining, with valuation still seen as supportive versus peers.

bullets.text: Escondida (BHP, Chile), the world's largest copper mine, is gradually resuming after the 23-Sep fatal-accident halt.
bullets.source: Kotak (Sumangal Nevatia) — Basic materials - daily news and prices (25-Sep)

detail.summary: Two consecutive Kotak news sweeps carry the arc: the 24-Sep sweep flagged the halt at the world's largest copper mine after a worker fatality, and the 25-Sep sweep (Reuters) reports operations gradually resuming, so the supply disruption to copper looks short-lived.

bullets.text: Indian copper producers seek a GST cut to 5% as record copper prices lock up working capital (Business Line).
bullets.source: Kotak (Sumangal Nevatia) — Basic materials - daily news and prices (+1 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: The ask targets GST relief for domestic copper producers whose working-capital needs have risen with record prices; a favourable outcome would help Hindustan Copper's cash cycle.

bullets.text: JPM downgrades Cyient DLM, Avalon & Syrma to UW; ROCE-vs-P/E ranking: Dixon > Amber > Kaynes > Syrma > Avalon > Cyient DLM.
bullets.source: JPM — India EMS: ROCEs matter for P/E multiples; downgrade Cyient DLM, Avalon, Syrma to UW

detail.summary: JPM argues EMS P/E multiples must reflect ROCE given capex-intensive, high-NWC businesses; Cyient DLM/Avalon/Syrma rallied 38%/35%/21% in six weeks on semiconductor optimism and now trade richer than Dixon despite lower ROCE. Reverse DCF implies 39%/37%/34% ten-year revenue CAGRs, which JPM calls too optimistic.

bullets.text: JPM keeps Avalon UW, PT Rs1,650 vs Rs2,316 CMP; management holds 3-yr revenue-doubling guide (~26% CAGR), gross margin 33-35%.
bullets.source: JPM — Avalon Technologies: Growth and margin guide maintained

detail.summary: JPM reiterates UW after hosting Avalon at its India Conference; management keeps the 3-year revenue-doubling guide and the 33-35% gross-margin band intact. Reverse DCF implies a 37% 10-year CAGR priced into the 52x 2-year forward PE.
points: Export mix target: US 30%, EU 10%, SE Asia 10%

bullets.text: IIFL upgrades Tata Technologies to BUY, TP Rs840 (from Rs780, 17% upside) on deal pipeline and 22% FY26-28 EPS growth.
bullets.source: IIFL — Tata Technologies [TATATECH IN, Upgrade to BUY]: Strong growth prospects; attractive entry point!

detail.summary: IIFL upgrades on a firing deal engine — two full-vehicle programmes converted, four more in the pipeline, plus the $100mn+ Tenneco deal — and calls the ~20% correction from peak an attractive entry point.
points: TP Rs840 from Rs780, 17% upside (33x 2YF P/E)
Four more full-vehicle deals in pipeline

bullets.text: JPM stays OW on Cyient; management targets EBIT margin 13.2% to 14-15% medium-term on HSD DET growth.
bullets.source: JPM — Cyient: Optimistic on both growth and margins

detail.summary: JPM's conference hosting of Cyient's Vice Chairman and CFO reinforces the Overweight: HSD DET growth on Aero MRO/after-market traction and a Telecom shift to network management, with margins climbing as the large-deal strategy matures.
points: 3Q wage hikes offset by other levers
HSD revenue growth targeted in DET
Aero growth from MRO and after-market

bullets.text: JPM Neutral on LTTS (PT Rs3,300): EU Auto growth limited, but mid-16% EBIT margin target by 4QFY27 reiterated.
bullets.source: JPM — L&T Technology Services: EU Auto under pressure, Sustianability strong, margin guide maintained (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: EU Auto OEMs are cutting engineering spend and pushing vendor consolidation/offshoring, while Sustainability keeps double-digit growth on plant modernisation; management reiterates the mid-16% margin target.
points: EU Auto growth limited; Chinese OEM competition

bullets.text: Brent +4.4% to $107.58/bbl on Hormuz phased-reopening talk; US 10Y +10bp to 5.22%, highest since 2007.
bullets.source: JPM — JPM Overnight Brief! 9/25 - Equities bouncing off the lows exploring a phased deal to reopen Hormuz

detail.summary: JPM frames a choppy session where equities bounced off lows on Hormuz reopening headlines while yields pushed to cycle highs on inflation and heavy issuance concerns; AI infra weakened on Oracle's Project Jupiter force-majeure headline.

bullets.text: UBS: Brent above $100 could widen India's CAD to ~2% of GDP and lift FY27 CPI to 5.5%; sees 50bp RBI hikes from October.
bullets.source: UBS — India "US$100+ Oil: What It Means for India"

detail.summary: UBS warns sustained $100+ Brent would squeeze OMC margins, risk retail fuel hikes and widen the twin deficits, keeping the RBI on a hiking path. Base case still assumes Brent averages $85/bbl in FY27.

bullets.text: FIIs net bought $260mn (cash+futures), DIIs $250mn on 23-Sep; Kotak expects weak overnight cues to reverse FII flows into a gap-down.
bullets.source: Kotak — Kotak : Insurance - Pretty Hard Draft ; Manipal - Initiate ADD ; Analyst Meets - VMM, Vinati, TECHM CALL (+3 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Kotak's morning flow note shows FIIs turned net buyers in cash and futures while retail trimmed index longs; overnight cues were expected to reverse the FII bid into a lower opening.

bullets.text: CLSA raises Hero MotoCorp TP to Rs6,685 (O-PF): 11x FY28CL core EPS vs 17x 10-yr average after an 11% monthly fall.
bullets.source: CLSA — Hero Motocorp (HMCL IB): What more is there to lose?

detail.summary: CLSA argues the commodity-fear sell-off created a mean-reversion opportunity, forecasting 8% EPS CAGR and ~4% dividend yield; Vida's e-2W losses are narrowing and the ~33% Ather Energy stake is a hidden value cushion.

bullets.text: Bharat Forge raised Rs20bn via QIP (10.6mn shares); report flags TVS Motor's link to the Chandrasekaran family.
bullets.source: Kotak — Kotak Auto News: Bharat Forge raises Rs20 bn through QIP; TVS link to Chandrasekaran's family raises questions

detail.summary: Kotak's daily auto roundup carries a Bharat Forge capital raise, a governance flag on TVS Motor's ties to the Tata Sons chairman's family, and Royal Enfield's new Classic 350 variant launch.
points: RE Classic 350 Signature White at Rs224k

bullets.text: IRDAI draft caps life EoM at 15% of GDPI in 2 years, 12.5% in 5; ICICI Sec sees PB Fintech most hit, SBI Life least.
bullets.source: ICICI Securities — India Insurance Consultation Paper: Pecking order of Impact (+1 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: IRDAI's 23-Sep consultation paper proposes hard commission caps and a company-level EoM glide path, comments due 25 October 2026; motor and closed-architecture bancassurance are least hit, open-market distributors most exposed.
points: General EoM 30% of GWP to 20% of GDPI
Motor TP commission to distributors nil
